J4M Full Roster PA/IP Analysis

1975–1989 · 352 team-seasons · real AAA and unused cards included · source audit completed with remaining estimates flagged

Updated October 8, 2026. Playing seasons 1975–1989; drafts 1976–1990. Every real rostered player counts, including real AAA and zero-use players. Sim-generated prospects and wrong-year transaction placeholders contribute no real-card capacity.

The corrected full-roster rerun still associates leaner pitching staffs and higher spending per useful card inning with better J4M draft results. Among the 312 team-seasons in the 24-team years, staffs at or below 1,400 card IP earned top-eight formula ranks 50.5% of the time; larger staffs did so 23.9% of the time. These are historical associations. The study does not establish that cutting a pitcher causes a better pick or that 1,400 IP is a safe fatigue target.

What changed and what is verified

The supplied ZIP contains 11,005 player/team/season rows covering all 352 team-seasons. All selected card keys, volumes and salaries match our local salary exports. The source's summed stints reproduce its 352 team totals within rounding. Our independent 1989 card reads agree with all 654 distinct real card identities represented in those checks; 748 source rows match because traded/preseason-listed players can have several team rows. All 26 earlier selected-card checks also agree.

Four wrong-team roster assignments were corrected from the original keeper/draft posts. Their rows remain in the audit trail at zero exposure. Two 1977 transaction dates were corrected from unique exact payroll changes and dated trade chronology. After these corrections, no player/role/season is allocated more than 162 roster games across teams. Salary-weighted card capacity is separate from official charged payroll; wins, Expected Wins, Score and earned formula ranks are unchanged.

Chicago 1977 illustrates why transaction order matters: the two affected pitchers raise the Thunderbears’ properly weighted card capacity from about 1,279 to 1,370 IP. Neither its actual record nor its draft rank changes.

Inputs and estimates that still limit the conclusions

191 positive-weight card rows retain inferred Full/Combined/Partial choices. Alternative-card ranges are displayed. They vary card selection while holding the supplied roster weights fixed; they do not cover every possible timing or roster error.

Seven trades use date estimates, because the 1981 sheet has only 21 identical salary records. The report separately shows the 24-team cohort excluding 1981.

29 positive-weight stints use fallback/inconsistent/multiple-team allocation, plus 10 remaining inferred salary-drop cut rows. The restricted sensitivity view excludes affected team-seasons, inferred cards and date-model exposure. It is a selected subset, not an unbiased replacement for the full league.

Two additional trade placements differ from independent payroll placement by one game (May 31,1977 and December 15,1986). They retain the source point estimate and remain qualified at that resolution.

The two source trades with blank game numbers contain only modern/generated placeholders, so they add no real PA/IP.

Payroll coverage gaps remain: 1975 source averaging covers 156/157 snapshots despite 162 raw rows; four 1977 team columns have 121 records; 1981 has 21 identical records; 1985 has one blank record per team. These limits affect salary-timing work independently of card matching.

The handoff supplies the previously missing full roster/stint evidence. It does not turn every inferred card, cut or calendar date into an observation. Raw ZIP/CSVs remain unchanged.

The example table supplied with this request has band counts 19/93/99/101. The current audited point estimates recalculate to 19/92/100/101; both total 312, with one fewer team in 1,300–1,400 IP and one more in 1,400–1,500 IP. This report uses the current canonical audited values. The combined ≤1,400 group is 111 teams (50.5% top 8); >1,400 is 201 teams (23.9% top 8).

No corrected point estimate in the 24-team cohort is at or below 1,200 IP; the smallest is 1,265. Across all 352 rows, the minimum is 1,258. We therefore have no identified ≤1,200 cohort from which to estimate a reliable win/pick rate. 1 team-season(s) can fall into that band under alternative unresolved card choices alone, so absence of a selected-card point case is not proof that a real sub 1,200 staff never existed.

A positive Score correlation points toward better formula draft position. Intervals resample whole seasons 1,000 times. Card IP/PA are available inputs; actual usage is an outcome and is not treated as a drafting lever. Unit cost partly reflects card quality and is not evidence that spending more by itself improves the pick. Owner-history correlation remains about 0.53 across 313 past-only observations within 1975–1989; it is persistent owner-associated performance, not a measured causal skill share.

Restricted sensitivity view

173 of 312 primary rows have no positive-weight inferred card, fallback/cut weight, or date-model exposure under the audit flags. Their correlations are in full_roster_restricted_sensitivity_correlations.csv. Exclusion can select owners and roster types unevenly; this is a sensitivity check, not a causal model or a guarantee of complete independent roster-date proof.

Files and source trail

Audited full roster/stints · All 352 teams and capacity metrics · Primary roster corrections · Trade game crosscheck

Independent payroll comes from the cached original annual Google Sheets; actual records, owners and league team IDs come from authorized WIS history reads. Selected-card snapshots and salary exports remain separately preserved. No account, team or source workbook changes.

Franchise histories

The 24 distinct clubs are connected by roster continuity across seasons. Houston/Brooklyn Thunderbears are older names of Chicago; the later Houston club is separate. Houston Hounds in 1984 stays credited to fabulous. Georgia continues through Minnetonka into Minnesota, and SoCal continues into Newark. The new historical reference includes the longer 1963–1989 record.
